Great - thanks for the fast reply, Miguel. Below is a proposed integration plan with sample routes and owners that should answer the streaming / function-calling questions. Vivek will lead the technical pairing; Neha will run success metrics collection.

Proposed integration plan (high-level):
1) Kickoff (60 min): keys, sample payloads, security checklist, runbook access.
2) Infrastructure & auth: create a scoped API key for the POC, configure IP allowlist for perf runs (if needed).
3) SDK integration: use Redwood SDK (Python or Node) to call the chat/generate endpoints. SDKs handle retries and chunk reassembly for streaming.
4) Streaming: two supported options - Server-Sent Events (SSE) over a standard HTTPS POST, or WebSockets for bi-directional. We'll default to SSE unless you need bi-directional websocket hooks.
5) Function/tool calling: Redwood supports structured function calls (JSON schema-driven). On function call, Redwood returns a dedicated JSON payload with arguments; you can invoke your enrichment webhook and return the result as a follow-up message.
6) Observability: enable token-level logs in the console, send sample traces to your tracing system via the tracing hook.

Example routes (high level):
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate (streaming via SSE with header Accept: text/event-stream)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/call-function (synchronous function call flow)
- WebSocket wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime?model=redwood-large (for low-latency bi-directional)

POC timeline (refined):
- Week 0 (kickoff): keys, runbook, sample dataset loaded
- Week 1: SDK + schema mapping + first-pass generation (owner: Diego + Vivek pairing)
- Week 2: Streaming + function-calling integration + perf runs (owner: Diego + SRE)
- Week 3: Evaluation runs, quality metrics collection (owner: Neha)
- Week 4: Wrap & recommendations (Marissa/Customer exec review)

Hi Miguel - Vivek here (SE). Quick technical notes and recommended defaults to make your eng ramp faster: 

1) SDKs & samples
- Python: pip install redwood-sdk
- Node: npm i @redwood/inference
- Sample (streaming SSE, simplified):
  POST /v1/chat/generate
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>, Accept: text/event-stream
  Body: { model: "redwood-large", messages: [{role: "user", content: "<input>"}], stream: true }
  Client: parse SSE events and stitch tokens as they arrive.

2) WebSockets vs SSE
- SSE: simplest to integrate for one-way streaming. Works with existing HTTP infrastructure and proxies.
- WebSockets: use when you need immediate bi-directional control (e.g., preemption or incremental tool responses).

3) Function / tool calling
- Redwood returns structured function_call objects (name + arguments JSON). Recommended flow:
  a) Redwood returns function_call for your enrichment webhook.
  b) Your service calls the enrichment webhook, returns result to your Redwood client as a follow-up message.
  c) Client posts the follow-up to /v1/chat/continue to resume generation with enrichment output.

4) Performance / batching tips
- For large batches, use continuous batching on the Redwood Dedicated path or increase concurrency windows in SDK.
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated product templates to reduce per-token compute.
- For perf runs, we'll coordinate an IP allowlist and synthetic traffic patterns with your SRE.

5) Security / auth
- Use scoped API keys with least privilege. For the POC, we can issue keys scoped to a single project and rotate them weekly.

6) Deliverables for kickoff
- Short runbook with sample payloads (redwood_poc_runbook.md)
- A pairing session (60-90m) to walk SDKs and run a sample streaming call live

I'll attach a short gist with code examples and a small checklist in the Drive folder. Please let me know Diego's availability for a 1:1 pairing session next week.

- Vivek
